subject: Tenant data fate & purge propagation for Hosted API

Subject: Question: how tenant data 'fate' gets enforced on Hosted API

Hi Karthik,

We're finalizing our security questionnaire and have a couple of precise questions about how Redwood handles 'tenant data fate' for the Hosted API. Two things in particular:

1) When a tenant requests permanent deletion of all their customer data (API logs, user inputs, KV cache), what are the end-to-end propagation windows across the different storage layers (live store, cache, backups) and how do you prove the data was removed?

2) If we rely on caching/TTL for performance, are there any guarantees we can rely on for sensitive tokens/PHI being evicted sooner? Any recommended config to reduce residual presence?

Would appreciate a short, clear answer we can paste into our RFP attachments.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Lambert
Head of Platform Security, Insalient

Subject: Re: Question: how tenant data 'fate' gets enforced on Hosted API

Hi Sophie — thanks for the questions, great ones. Answering at a high level here and attaching a simple data-flow diagram and a short retention summary; Marissa (security) and Vivek (ops) are cc'd for details and attestation language.

Summary (short):
- Deletion request intake: self-serve API or support ticket. For API-initiated tenant erasure we accept a signed request; for legal/D SARs we follow documented identity verification.
- Live data store: user/customer records and model inputs are deleted within 72 hours after request acceptance from the primary live store.
- KV/prefix cache: cache entries are evicted on request; typical propagation completes within 1–24 hours depending on TTL and shard caching. We offer a forced-evict API call which reduces this to under 1 hour for affected keys on most configurations.
- Backups & snapshots: incremental backups are pruned on a rolling schedule — deletion markers applied within 30 days; fully purged from long-term snapshots within 90 days in standard hosted plans (expedited purge available under enterprise SOW).
- Evidence / attestation: we provide a signed deletion confirmation (JSON) plus internal audit log export showing delete job IDs, timestamps, and operator/service IDs. For customers requiring an independent attestation we can provide SOC2-compatible logs and export of related audit records.

Recommendations to minimize residual presence:
- Use token-scoped prompts and avoid persisting PII in free-text fields; enable request-level masking (we can enable automatic redaction for specific patterns).
- Configure short cache TTLs (recommended 60–300 seconds) for endpoints that may see sensitive tokens. For throughput-sensitive routes we suggest prefix-aware caching with conservative TTLs and the forced-evict call documented in the attachment.
- Enable retention tags on saved prompts so purge jobs can target only non-essential artifacts.

Next steps: if you'd like, Marissa can provide sample attestation wording and a timeline SLA we can include in a DPA or SOW.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie — Marissa from Security here. Short answers inline below, followed by the formal language we recommend for an RFP/DPA clause.

- 72-hour window: confirmed — measured from request acceptance timestamp. The deletion workflow has a mandatory acceptance check (identity + integrity validation); we record acceptance time in the audit log and all SLA timers begin at that timestamp.

- Backups & expedited purge: we offer an expedited purge addendum for Enterprise customers. Typical lead time for expedited purge is 7–14 calendar days for full snapshot reconstitution and purge, costs vary by retention depth and region — ballpark estimates run 15–25k USD depending on snapshot footprint. We can provide a firm estimate after a footprint scan.

- Forced-evict API limits & cost: default rate limit is 60 evict calls/minute per tenant (can be increased via request and contractual changes). Evict calls are lightweight; we do not bill per-call for Enterprise customers but do meter them for smaller tiers to prevent abusive traffic. If you plan to integrate evict into a token sanitation pipeline we recommend batching keys where possible and discussing higher limits during onboarding.

Suggested RFP clause (copy/paste):
"Redwood Inference will honor tenant-initiated deletion requests for Hosted API customers. Deletions are accepted and scheduled upon verification; primary live-store artifacts are removed within seventy-two (72) hours of acceptance. Cache eviction is completed within one (1) hour when the Forced Eviction API is invoked; otherwise cache propagation may take up to twenty-four (24) hours depending on configured TTLs. Backups containing deleted artifacts will have deletion markers applied within thirty (30) days and will be purged from long-term snapshots within ninety (90) days, except where an expedited purge addendum is executed by the parties. Redwood will provide a signed deletion confirmation and export of the relevant audit logs within five (5) business days of final purge"

We've attached the diagram and a short retention summary (see attachments). If you'd like, Vivek can run a quick footprint scan and a sample expedited purge quote — Vivek, can you take that?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
